newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end higher with secondaries in lead.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end higher with secondaries in lead.

text.p: Retail investors, including syndicates, piled back into Malaysian secondary shares on Thursday, while blue chips attracted moderate interest from local and regional funds, dealers said.

At the close, the Composite Index of 100 leading stocks was up 12.41 points or 1.17 percent to 1,071.03. The Second Board index of smaller-capitalisation shares surged 20.38 points, or 3.74 percent, to 564.98.
"It's mainly been local funds on the buy side," said Ralph Dixon, of TA Securities' international division. "I do think the upside is fairly capped," he added.
Analysts said sentiment was still shaky as the market tries to steady itself from almost two months of selling.

A Bank Negara move to curtail loans to the property sector and restrict loans for stock purchases announced at the end of March jolted the market. Sentiment was further dented by Thailand's property crisis and economic slowdown.

From March 28 to May 16, the market capitalisation of the Composite Index dropped by 56.45 billion ringgit to 316.22 billion ringgit. The Second Board index has shed 14.45 billion ringgit in capitalisation to 55.29 billion ringgit over the same period.
Shares of financial firms MBf Capital and Suria Holdings remained in strong demand despite no official confirmation of takeover talks.
MBf Capital chief executive officer Loy Hean Heang said, however, that "if there is an opportunity we will be very pleased to discuss (it)".
MBf Capital jumped 42 cents to 5.30 ringgit, while Suria gained 19 cents to 2.86 ringgit.

Renong Bhd added 20 cents to 3.40 ringgit. Dealers said investors were coming back into the stock following last week's denial that Renong's United Engineers (M) Bhd would buy a stake in loss-making National Steel Corp of the Philippines.
"We're seeing selected institutional buying in stocks like Renong and Maybank," said an institutional dealer with a local brokerage.
Total market volume topped 323 million shares, valued at 2.4 billion ringgit, with gainers swamping losers by 595 to 59.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot May contract ended up nine points at 1,062, with 1,227 contracts traded. The June contract gained 9.3 points to 1,064.8 with turnover of 231 lots.
